title: Folded Hands Emoji 🙏 Meaning: Prayer, Thanks or High Five?
description: 🙏 means please, thank you or praying for you, and it is not a high five. Learn where the folded hands emoji comes from and how its meaning shifts by culture.
summary: The 🙏 folded hands emoji means please, thank you, or prayer. People send it to show gratitude, to ask for a favor, to hope hard for an outcome, or to offer prayers and sympathy. It depicts one person's two palms pressed together, not two people high-fiving.
meaning: Three meanings dominate. The first is gratitude: “thank you so much 🙏” is warmer and humbler than the words alone. The second is pleading or hoping, as in “please let this bus come 🙏.” The third is prayer in the religious sense, used when someone is sick, grieving or facing something hard. Which one applies is almost always clear from the sentence around it.

The emoji comes from Japanese phone carriers' original sets, and in Japan pressed palms are an everyday gesture for “please,” “thank you” and “sorry,” including the moment before a meal. That origin explains why the Unicode name is the neutral “folded hands” rather than “praying hands.” Western users mapped it onto Christian prayer, while many South Asian users read it as namaste, the palms-together greeting.

The high-five theory resurfaces online every few years. It is a misreading: the thumbs sit on the same side, the sleeves on most designs match, and the emoji's documented purpose is the gesture of thanks or prayer. That said, enough people have used it for a celebratory hand slap that the recipient may understand it that way in the right context.

Tone has broadened with use. In wellness and yoga circles it signals calm or respect. In casual slang it expresses reverence for something excellent (“that album 🙏”). Athletes and musicians post it after wins or injuries as shorthand for feeling blessed or asking for support. It is also one of the most used emojis in condolence messages worldwide.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Everyday use is mostly thanks and requests. “Can you grab my package? 🙏” softens the ask; “you're a lifesaver 🙏” deepens the thanks. Repeating it, 🙏🙏🙏, adds urgency or desperation, often jokingly, as in begging a friend to share their notes. Following bad news, it shifts to “I'm thinking of you” or “praying for you.”

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: In comments under announcements of illness, loss or disaster, rows of 🙏 stand in for prayers and solidarity. Under good news, it reads as “blessed” or “grateful.” Creators also use it to thank followers for milestones. On music and sports posts it frequently means respect, a quiet bow toward someone's talent or effort.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It is a common and accepted way to say thanks in advance or to acknowledge a favor in workplace chat, particularly on international teams. Because some readers see it as explicitly religious, a few people prefer plainer options in formal messages. As a reaction to a colleague's help, it is generally understood simply as appreciation.

contexts.label: Around the world
contexts.body: In India and much of South and Southeast Asia, palms together is a greeting and a sign of respect, so 🙏 can simply mean hello or goodbye. In Japan it covers thanks, apology and requests. In majority-Christian countries the prayer reading comes first. Muslims more often use 🤲 for supplication, since open, raised palms match the posture of dua.

examples.text: Thank you for covering my shift 🙏
examples.meaning: Sincere gratitude with a note of humility.

examples.text: Please please let me borrow the car tonight 🙏🙏
examples.meaning: Playful begging; the sender really wants a yes.

examples.text: Surgery is tomorrow morning. Keep her in your thoughts 🙏
examples.meaning: A request for prayers or good wishes during a serious moment.
Hoping for a good outcome that is now out of the sender's hands.
Reverence: the sender is bowing down to how good it was.

examples.text: Namaste 🙏 see you all in class Thursday
examples.meaning: A respectful greeting or sign-off, common in yoga and South Asian contexts.

combos.meaning: Heartfelt thanks or loving support, common in condolence and get-well messages.
Manifesting or wishing for something good; hopeful rather than solemn.
Overwhelmed gratitude, or desperate pleading, depending on the sentence.
Hoping and praying at once, used while waiting on results or news.

confusedWith.difference: 🤲 shows open, cupped palms facing up, the posture of Islamic dua and of receiving or offering something. 🙏 presses the palms together, which reads as Christian prayer, namaste or thanks. Both can mean prayer, but in different traditions.
🙌 lifts both hands in celebration or praise: hooray, hallelujah, yes! 🙏 is quieter, expressing thanks, hope or a request. If a high five is what you mean, 🙌 or ✋ fits better than folded hands.
🙇 shows a whole person bowing deeply, used for strong apology, begging or deference in the Japanese sense. 🙏 is only the hands and leans toward thanks and prayer more than apology.

avoid: Do not use it as a breezy “thanks” right after someone shares something tragic unless you mean prayers or sympathy, since the tone can blur.
Avoid assuming it reads as a high five; most recipients will see prayer or gratitude.
Hold back in formal messages to people who may not welcome religious overtones.
design: Two hands pressed flat together, fingers pointing up, usually with a bit of sleeve at each wrist. Today's designs from Apple, Google, Samsung and Microsoft look alike. Older versions varied more: Apple's early artwork had rays of light bursting from behind the hands, and Google's Android once drew a small person with palms together instead of just the hands.

faqs.q: Is 🙏 a high five or praying hands?
faqs.a: It is folded hands, meaning prayer, please or thank you. The high-five idea is a popular internet myth. The emoji came from Japanese sets where pressed palms express gratitude and requests, and both hands belong to one person.

faqs.q: What does 🙏 mean from a guy or a girl?
faqs.a: It carries no romantic meaning from anyone. It usually says thank you, please or “hoping for the best.” After you share something difficult, it signals support. It is respectful rather than flirty.

faqs.q: Is the folded hands emoji religious?
faqs.a: It can be but does not have to be. Many people use it for prayer in Christian, Hindu, Buddhist and other traditions, while just as many use it secularly for thanks or pleading. Its official name deliberately avoids mentioning prayer.

It represents the palms-together gesture used to say please, thank you or sorry, and the pose made with “itadakimasu” before eating. Japanese users read it as polite gratitude or apology far more than as religious prayer.

faqs.q: Can I use 🙏 to say namaste?
faqs.a: Yes. The gesture matches the Indian greeting in which palms are pressed together, often with a slight bow. Many South Asian users send it as a respectful hello, goodbye or thank you in exactly that sense.
